answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer:
No, please do not add the two missed runs, and do not try to run all three days next week (Sep 14 – 20). Treat Wednesday and Saturday as a return, not a catch-up, and only run if you have no fever and feel well enough.

Go back to three runs a week, Monday, Wednesday and Saturday, once the cough has cleared and you have had a few good days in a row.

new.analysis:
Last week was a partial week, and the gap came from illness rather than from choice. Monday went as planned: you ran 2.78 km in 23 minutes 59 seconds at effort 6/10, with heart rate averaging 139. The cold turned into a fever on Wednesday night, which is why the Wednesday and Saturday runs did not happen.

This week is mostly rest because you still have a cough and a blocked nose, and you describe yourself as wiped out. Running hard through that asks your body to fight the cold and carry training at the same time. Two short runs keep the habit going without adding load.

Build phase normally adds threshold work, but I am holding that back for now. Your runs are still walk-run at an easy effort, and a fast session right after an illness would add stress with little gain. Harder running can come once you can run 20 minutes without a walk break.

The two runs this week are shorter than the ones you missed, 20 and 22 minutes against 24 and 27. That keeps the load close to where it was before the cold rather than above it. Keeping heart rate under 140 holds the effort easy while you rebuild.

The race is still possible in eight weeks, but only with steady running from next week onward. This week also doubles as the lighter week the build calls for, since the illness already forced one. Consistent short runs will do more for you than a single long catch-up session.

I cannot judge how the illness is progressing from here. Let how you feel decide each run, and see a doctor or pharmacist if the fever returns or the cough drags on.
